item.title: Idioms for debate
item.description: Advanced idioms for discussion, argument and opinion.

children.definition: a question that is open to debate, or no longer worth discussing because it makes no difference
children.example: Whether we could have won is a moot point now.

children.definition: something that has both good and bad effects
children.example: Working from home can be a double-edged sword.

children.definition: an obvious problem that everyone avoids talking about
children.example: The budget cut was the elephant in the room at the meeting.
children.translation_uz: hamma biladigan, lekin tilga olinmaydigan muammo

children.definition: a result that is certain even before it happens
children.example: With their best player injured, defeat seemed a foregone conclusion.

children.definition: something that takes attention away from the real issue
children.example: The question of cost is a red herring; the real problem is time.

children.definition: to argue about very small, unimportant differences
children.example: Let's not split hairs over the exact wording.

children.definition: to say you support something without doing anything to help it
children.example: Many firms pay lip service to work–life balance.

children.definition: to make a situation more confusing or less clear
children.example: Adding a third option only muddied the waters.

children.definition: a task or request that is very difficult to achieve
children.example: Finishing the whole report by tomorrow is a tall order.

children.definition: for the same reason; following the same logic
children.example: If you expect honesty from your team, by the same token you must be honest with them.
children.translation_ru: по той же причине, точно так же

children.definition: a personal reason, often financial, for wanting something to happen
children.example: The study was paid for by a company with a vested interest in the result.

children.definition: to make yourself do something unpleasant that you have been avoiding
children.example: I finally bit the bullet and booked a dentist appointment.
